I am a CS undergraduate from LUMS aspiring to pursue Graduate opportunities anywhere in the world with good compute :) and even better peers/mentors.

Currently, I am serving as a Teaching Fellow (junior faculty position) at the CS department of LUMS. 

My day usually has me acting on two fronts: 

**Researching**: I lead two research groups, one at CSALT and one at City Lab. Underneath the glamour, I sit on my PC and make slightly non-trivial attempts at answering

*How can we distill knowledge from Teacher to Student in a low loss manner? Can we isolate knowledge circuits in Teachers and distill these circuits into Students?*

**Teaching**: I currently co-teach the data-structures course to a class of over 300 students (yes I know thats a lot of students). Previously, I taught the MS-AI bootcamp, a crash-course for going over programming basics and mathematical foundations of AI for incoming graduate students (most of them were from non-technical backgrounds).

___

## My Research Interests

- **Model Compression:**
It started of with *KV cache compression* but right now, I am entranced by *Knowledge Distillation* - the goal is to build a *hive mind*.

- **Mechanistic Interpretability:**
Ever since I came across [Neel Nanda's](https://www.neelnanda.io/) work, I have been fascinated by our ability to *reverse engineer* DNNs even as complex as LLMs! Specifically, I am focusing on *isolating circuits* in large models.

- **Reasoning LLMs:**
Currently, to inculcate reasoning in smaller models (students) using large reasoning models (teachers), we do *SFT on reasoning traces* of teachers or a variant of it.
<div style="text-align: center;">
I am currently working with my research group to unlock a new *circuit distillation approach* that first *isolates and then distills reasoning circuits*.
</div>
